questions.text: Where will the device be installed? Does the wall box have mains live AND neutral wires, or only the two wires to the boiler or valves?
options: Live and neutral are in the box: power it from mains (recommended: instant remote control, no battery changes, about $4 more)
Battery only, even if mains is present
No neutral in the box (only switched wires): battery is required
questions.why: On a battery the device must sleep and can contact Wi-Fi only about once an hour to last a year. Kept connected, it lasts about 3 weeks. Mains power removes that limit (conflicts.md C1).

questions.text: If it runs on battery: when you change a setting from your phone, how long can it take to apply?
options: Up to 60 minutes, 1 AA lasts about 13 months alkaline or 2 years lithium (recommended)
Up to 15 minutes, a lithium AA lasts about 8 months (misses the 1-year goal)
Up to 5 minutes, a battery lasts 6 to 12 weeks
questions.why: Each Wi-Fi check costs about 0.5 J, and one AA holds about 6.7 kJ usable. Temperature control and the schedule work locally in every case (conflicts.md C1).

questions.text: What will each of the two outputs switch on and off?
options: 230 V thermal valve heads or zone valves, up to 2 A each (recommended)
A boiler or a circulation pump at 230 V, up to 5 A
Only the boiler's low-voltage thermostat contact (no 230 V)
A mix, or I do not know
questions.why: This sets the relay rating and whether 230 V enters the box. Without 230 V, the safety insulation and size problems become much smaller (conflicts.md C4, C5).

questions.text: Where do the two temperature probes go?
options: One at the device, the other on a cable up to 10 m to the second room (recommended)
Both on cables up to 10 m
Both rooms are next to the box, cables shorter than 2 m
The second room needs a probe more than 10 m away
questions.why: A long probe cable picks up mains hum. If it shares a conduit with 230 V wires, it must be a mains-rated cable (conflicts.md C6).
